text:
अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम्।

संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते।।2.34।।
text_kannada:
ಅಕೀರ್ತಿಂ ಚಾಪಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ಕಥಯಿಷ್ಯಂತಿ ತೇಽವ್ಯಯಾಮ್ |
ಸಂಭಾವಿತಸ್ಯ ಚಾಕೀರ್ತಿರ್ಮರಣಾದತಿರಿಚ್ಯತೇ || ೩೪ ||
text_telugu:
అకీర్తిం చాపి భూతాని కథయిష్యంతి తేఽవ్యయామ్ |
సంభావితస్య చాకీర్తిర్మరణాదతిరిచ్యతే || ౩౪ ||
transliteration:
akīrtiṁ chāpi bhūtāni
kathayiṣhyanti te ’vyayām
sambhāvitasya chākīrtir
maraṇād atirichyate
translation_english: People also will speak of your unending infamy, and to an honored person, infamy is worse than death.
context_english: akīrtim—infamy; cha—and; api—also; bhūtāni—people; kathayiṣhyanti—will speak; te—of your; avyayām—everlasting; sambhāvitasya—of a respectable person; cha—and; akīrtiḥ—infamy; maraṇāt—than death; atirichyate—is greater

text:
भयाद्रणादुपरतं मंस्यन्ते त्वां महारथाः।

येषां च त्वं बहुमतो भूत्वा यास्यसि लाघवम्।।2.35।।
text_kannada:
ಭಯಾದ್ರಣಾದುಪರತಂ ಮಂಸ್ಯಂತೇ ತ್ವಾಂ ಮಹಾರಥಾಃ |
ಯೇಷಾಂ ಚ ತ್ವಂ ಬಹುಮತೋ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಯಾಸ್ಯಸಿ ಲಾಘವಮ್ || ೩೫ ||
text_telugu:
భయాద్రణాదుపరతం మంస్యంతే త్వాం మహారథాః |
యేషాం చ త్వం బహుమతో భూత్వా యాస్యసి లాఘవమ్ || ౩౫ ||
transliteration:
bhayād raṇād uparataṁ mansyante tvāṁ mahā-rathāḥ
yeṣhāṁ cha tvaṁ bahu-mato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
translation_english: The great chariot-riders will think of you as having desisted from the fight out of fear, and you will fall into disgrace before them whom you had been estimable to.
context_english: bhayāt—out of fear; raṇāt—from the battlefield; uparatam—have fled; maṁsyante—will think; tvām—you; mahā-rathāḥ—warriors who could single handedly match the strength of ten thousand ordinary warriors; yeṣhām—for whom; cha—and; tvam—you; bahu-mataḥ—high esteemed; bhūtvā—having been; yāsyasi—you will loose; lāghavam—decreased in value

text:
अवाच्यवादांश्च बहून् वदिष्यन्ति तवाहिताः।

निन्दन्तस्तव सामर्थ्यं ततो दुःखतरं नु किम्।।2.36।।
text_kannada:
ಅವಾಚ್ಯವಾದಾಂಶ್ಚ ಬಹೂನ್ ವದಿಷ್ಯಂತಿ ತವಾಹಿತಾಃ |
ನಿಂದಂತಸ್ತವ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಂ ತತೋ ದುಃಖತರಂ ನು ಕಿಮ್ || ೩೬ ||
text_telugu:
అవాచ్యవాదాంశ్చ బహూన్ వదిష్యంతి తవాహితాః |
నిందంతస్తవ సామర్థ్యం తతో దుఃఖతరం ను కిమ్ || ౩౬ ||
transliteration:
avāchya-vādānśh cha bahūn vadiṣhyanti tavāhitāḥ
nindantastava sāmarthyaṁ tato duḥkhataraṁ nu kim
translation_english: And your enemies will speak many indecent words while denigrating your power. What can be more painful than that?
context_english: avāchya-vādān—using harsh words; cha—and; bahūn—many; vadiṣhyanti—will say; tava—your; ahitāḥ—enemies; nindantaḥ—defame; tava—your; sāmarthyam—might; tataḥ—than that; duḥkha-taram—more painful; nu—indeed; kim—what

text:
हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्।

तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः।।2.37।।
text_kannada:
ಹತೋ ವಾ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಂ ಜಿತ್ವಾ ವಾ ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಸೇ ಮಹೀಮ್ |
ತಸ್ಮಾದುತ್ತಿಷ್ಠ ಕೌಂತೇಯ ಯುದ್ಧಾಯ ಕೃತನಿಶ್ಚಯಃ || ೩೭ ||
text_telugu:
హతో వా ప్రాప్స్యసి స్వర్గం జిత్వా వా భోక్ష్యసే మహీమ్ |
తస్మాదుత్తిష్ఠ కౌంతేయ యుద్ధాయ కృతనిశ్చయః || ౩౭ ||
transliteration:
hato vā prāpsyasi swargaṁ jitvā vā bhokṣhyase mahīm
tasmād uttiṣhṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛita-niśhchayaḥ
translation_english: Either by being killed, you will attain heaven, or by winning, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, O Arjuna, rise up with determination to fight.
context_english: hataḥ—slain; vā—or; prāpsyasi—you will attain; swargam—celestial abodes; jitvā—by achieving victory; vā—or; bhokṣhyase—you shall enjoy; mahīm—the kingdom on earth; tasmāt—therefore; uttiṣhṭha—arise; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; yuddhāya—for fight; kṛita-niśhchayaḥ—with determination

text:
सुखदुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ।

ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि।।2.38।।
text_kannada:
ಸುಖದುಃಖೇ ಸಮೇ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ಲಾಭಾಲಾಭೌ ಜಯಾಜಯೌ |
ತತೋ ಯುದ್ಧಾಯ ಯುಜ್ಯಸ್ವ ನೈವಂ ಪಾಪಮವಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ || ೩೮ ||
text_telugu:
సుఖదుఃఖే సమే కృత్వా లాభాలాభౌ జయాజయౌ |
తతో యుద్ధాయ యుజ్యస్వ నైవం పాపమవాప్స్యసి || ౩౮ ||
transliteration:
sukha-duḥkhe same kṛitvā lābhālābhau jayājayau
tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṁ pāpam avāpsyasi
translation_english: Treating happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, and conquest and defeat with equanimity, then engage in battle. Thus, you will not incur sin.
context_english: sukha—happiness; duḥkhe—in distress; same kṛitvā—treating alike; lābha-alābhau—gain and loss; jaya-ajayau—victory and defeat; tataḥ—thereafter; yuddhāya—for fighting; yujyasva—engage; na—never; evam—thus; pāpam—sin; avāpsyasi—shall incur

text:
एषा तेऽभिहिता सांख्ये बुद्धिर्योगे त्विमां श्रृणु।

बुद्ध्यायुक्तो यया पार्थ कर्मबन्धं प्रहास्यसि।।2.39।।
text_kannada:
ಏಷಾ ತೇಽಭಿಹಿತಾ ಸಾಂಖ್ಯೇ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ಯೋಗೇ ತ್ವಿಮಾಂ ಶ್ರೃಣು |
ಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾಯುಕ್ತೋ ಯಯಾ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಕರ್ಮಬಂಧಂ ಪ್ರಹಾಸ್ಯಸಿ || ೩೯ ||
text_telugu:
ఏషా తేఽభిహితా సాంఖ్యే బుద్ధిర్యోగే త్విమాం శ్రృణు |
బుద్ధ్యాయుక్తో యయా పార్థ కర్మబంధం ప్రహాస్యసి || ౩౯ ||
transliteration:
eṣhā te ’bhihitā sānkhye
buddhir yoge tvimāṁ śhṛiṇu
buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha
karma-bandhaṁ prahāsyasi
translation_english: O Partha, this wisdom has been imparted to you from the standpoint of Self-realization. But listen to this wisdom from the standpoint of Yoga, endowed with which, you will get rid of the bondage of action.
context_english: eṣhā—hitherto; te—to you; abhihitā—explained; sānkhye—by analytical knowledge; buddhiḥ yoge—by the yog of intellect; tu—indeed; imām—this; śhṛiṇu—listen; buddhyā—by understanding; yuktaḥ—united; yayā—by which; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; karma-bandham—bondage of karma; prahāsyasi—you shall be released from

text:
नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते।

स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात्।।2.40।।
text_kannada:
ನೇಹಾಭಿಕ್ರಮನಾಶೋಽಸ್ತಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯವಾಯೋ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ |
ಸ್ವಲ್ಪಮಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಧರ್ಮಸ್ಯ ತ್ರಾಯತೇ ಮಹತೋ ಭಯಾತ್ || ೪೦ ||
text_telugu:
నేహాభిక్రమనాశోఽస్తి ప్రత్యవాయో న విద్యతే |
స్వల్పమప్యస్య ధర్మస్య త్రాయతే మహతో భయాత్ || ౪౦ ||
transliteration:
nehābhikrama-nāśho ’sti pratyavāyo na vidyate
svalpam apyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
translation_english: Here, there is no waste of effort; nor is there any harm. Even a little of this righteousness saves one from great fear.
context_english: na—not; iha—in this; abhikrama—efforts; nāśhaḥ—loss; asti—there is; pratyavāyaḥ—adverse result; na—not; vidyate—is; su-alpam—a little; api—even; asya—of this; dharmasya—occupation; trāyate—saves; mahataḥ—from great; bhayāt—danger

text:
व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।

बहुशाखा ह्यनन्ताश्च बुद्धयोऽव्यवसायिनाम्।।2.41।।
text_kannada:
ವ್ಯವಸಾಯಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿರೇಕೇಹ ಕುರುನಂದನ |
ಬಹುಶಾಖಾ ಹ್ಯನಂತಾಶ್ಚ ಬುದ್ಧಯೋಽವ್ಯವಸಾಯಿನಾಮ್ || ೪೧ ||
text_telugu:
వ్యవసాయాత్మికా బుద్ధిరేకేహ కురునందన |
బహుశాఖా హ్యనంతాశ్చ బుద్ధయోఽవ్యవసాయినామ్ || ౪౧ ||
transliteration:
vyavasāyātmikā buddhir ekeha kuru-nandana
bahu-śhākhā hyanantāśh cha buddhayo ’vyavasāyinām
translation_english: O scion of the Kuru dynasty, in this there is a single, one-pointed conviction. The thoughts of the irresolute ones, however, have many branches indeed and are innumerable.
context_english: vyavasāya-ātmikā—resolute; buddhiḥ—intellect; ekā—single; iha—on this path; kuru-nandana—descendent of the Kurus; bahu-śhākhāḥ—many-branched; hi—indeed; anantāḥ—endless; cha—also; buddhayaḥ—intellect; avyavasāyinām—of the irresolute

text:
यामिमां पुष्पितां वाचं प्रवदन्त्यविपश्चितः।

वेदवादरताः पार्थ नान्यदस्तीति वादिनः।।2.42।।
text_kannada:
ಯಾಮಿಮಾಂ ಪುಷ್ಪಿತಾಂ ವಾಚಂ ಪ್ರವದಂತ್ಯವಿಪಶ್ಚಿತಃ |
ವೇದವಾದರತಾಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ನಾನ್ಯದಸ್ತೀತಿ ವಾದಿನಃ || ೪೨ ||
text_telugu:
యామిమాం పుష్పితాం వాచం ప్రవదంత్యవిపశ్చితః |
వేదవాదరతాః పార్థ నాన్యదస్తీతి వాదినః || ౪౨ ||
transliteration:
yāmimāṁ puṣhpitāṁ vāchaṁ pravadanty-avipaśhchitaḥ
veda-vāda-ratāḥ pārtha nānyad astīti vādinaḥ
 kāmātmānaḥ swarga-parā janma-karma-phala-pradām
kriyā-viśheṣha-bahulāṁ bhogaiśhwarya-gatiṁ prati
translation_english: O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk, which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence, remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as their goal.
context_english:
yām imām—all these; puṣhpitām—flowery; vācham—words; pravadanti—speak; avipaśhchitaḥ—those with limited understanding; veda-vāda-ratāḥ—attached to the flowery words of the Vedas; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; na anyat—no other; asti—is; iti—thus; vādinaḥ—advocate;
 kāma-ātmānaḥ—desirous of sensual pleasure; swarga-parāḥ—aiming to achieve the heavenly planets; janma-karma-phala—high birth and fruitive results; pradāṁ—awarding; kriyā-viśheṣha—pompous ritualistic ceremonies; bahulām—various; bhoga—gratification; aiśhwarya—luxury; gatim—progress; prati—toward

text:
कामात्मानः स्वर्गपरा जन्मकर्मफलप्रदाम्।

क्रियाविशेषबहुलां भोगैश्वर्यगतिं प्रति।।2.43।।
text_kannada:
ಕಾಮಾತ್ಮಾನಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಪರಾ ಜನ್ಮಕರ್ಮಫಲಪ್ರದಾಮ್ |
ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಶೇಷಬಹುಲಾಂ ಭೋಗೈಶ್ವರ್ಯಗತಿಂ ಪ್ರತಿ || ೪೩ ||
text_telugu:
కామాత్మానః స్వర్గపరా జన్మకర్మఫలప్రదామ్ |
క్రియావిశేషబహులాం భోగైశ్వర్యగతిం ప్రతి || ౪౩ ||
transliteration:
kāmātmānaḥ svarga-parā 

 janma-karma-phala-pradām

 kriyā-viśeṣa-bahulāṁ

 bhogaiśvarya-gatiṁ prati
translation_english: O son of Prtha, those undiscerning people who utter this flowery talk, which promises birth as a result of rites and duties, and is full of various special rites meant for the attainment of enjoyment and affluence, remain engrossed in the utterances of the Vedas and declare that nothing else exists; their minds are full of desires and they have heaven as their goal.
context_english: kāmaātmānaḥ—desirous   of  sense   gratification;  svarga-parāḥ—aiming to  achieve heavenly    planets;    janma-karma-phala-pradām—resulting  in  fruitive    action, good        birth,     etc.;      kriyā-viśeṣa—pompous       ceremonies;        bahulām—various; bhoga—sense       enjoyment;     aiśvarya—opulence;     gatim—progress;    prati—towards.

text:
भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्।

व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते।।2.44।।
text_kannada:
ಭೋಗೈಶ್ವರ್ಯಪ್ರಸಕ್ತಾನಾಂ ತಯಾಪಹೃತಚೇತಸಾಮ್ |
ವ್ಯವಸಾಯಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿಃ ಸಮಾಧೌ ನ ವಿಧೀಯತೇ || ೪೪ ||
text_telugu:
భోగైశ్వర్యప్రసక్తానాం తయాపహృతచేతసామ్ |
వ్యవసాయాత్మికా బుద్ధిః సమాధౌ న విధీయతే || ౪౪ ||
transliteration:
bhogaiśwvarya-prasaktānāṁ tayāpahṛita-chetasām
vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
translation_english: One-pointed conviction does not become established in the minds of those who delight in enjoyment and affluence, and whose intellects are carried away by it.
context_english: bhoga—gratification; aiśhwarya—luxury; prasaktānām—whose minds are deeply attached; tayā—by that; apahṛita-chetasām—bewildered in intellect; vyavasāya-ātmikā—resolute; buddhiḥ—intellect; samādhau—fulfilment; na—never; vidhīyate—occurs

text:
त्रैगुण्यविषया वेदा निस्त्रैगुण्यो भवार्जुन।

निर्द्वन्द्वो नित्यसत्त्वस्थो निर्योगक्षेम आत्मवान्।।2.45।।
text_kannada:
ತ್ರೈಗುಣ್ಯವಿಷಯಾ ವೇದಾ ನಿಸ್ತ್ರೈಗುಣ್ಯೋ ಭವಾರ್ಜುನ |
ನಿರ್ದ್ವಂದ್ವೋ ನಿತ್ಯಸತ್ತ್ವಸ್ಥೋ ನಿರ್ಯೋಗಕ್ಷೇಮ ಆತ್ಮವಾನ್ || ೪೫ ||
text_telugu:
త్రైగుణ్యవిషయా వేదా నిస్త్రైగుణ్యో భవార్జున |
నిర్ద్వంద్వో నిత్యసత్త్వస్థో నిర్యోగక్షేమ ఆత్మవాన్ || ౪౫ ||
transliteration:
trai-guṇya-viṣhayā vedā nistrai-guṇyo bhavārjuna
nirdvandvo nitya-sattva-stho niryoga-kṣhema ātmavān
translation_english: O Arjuna, the Vedas [Meaning only the portion dealing with rites and duties (karma-kanda).] have the three qualities as their object. You become free from worldliness, free from the pairs of duality, ever-poised in the quality of sattva, without (desire for) acquisition and protection, and self-collected.
context_english: trai-guṇya—of the three modes of material nature; viṣhayāḥ—subject matter; vedāḥ—Vedic scriptures; nistrai-guṇyaḥ—above the three modes of material nature, transcendental; bhava—be; arjuna—Arjun; nirdvandvaḥ—free from dualities; nitya-sattva-sthaḥ—eternally fixed in truth; niryoga-kṣhemaḥ—unconcerned about gain and preservation; ātma-vān—situated in the self

text:
यावानर्थ उदपाने सर्वतः संप्लुतोदके।

तावान्सर्वेषु वेदेषु ब्राह्मणस्य विजानतः।।2.46।।
text_kannada:
ಯಾವಾನರ್ಥ ಉದಪಾನೇ ಸರ್ವತಃ ಸಂಪ್ಲುತೋದಕೇ |
ತಾವಾನ್ಸರ್ವೇಷು ವೇದೇಷು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಸ್ಯ ವಿಜಾನತಃ || ೪೬ ||
text_telugu:
యావానర్థ ఉదపానే సర్వతః సంప్లుతోదకే |
తావాన్సర్వేషు వేదేషు బ్రాహ్మణస్య విజానతః || ౪౬ ||
transliteration:
yāvān artha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake
tāvānsarveṣhu vedeṣhu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
translation_english: A Brahmana with realization has that much utility in all the Vedas as a person has in a well when there is a flood all around.
context_english: yāvān—whatever; arthaḥ—purpose; uda-pāne—a well of water; sarvataḥ—in all respects; sampluta-udake—by a large lake; tāvān—that many; sarveṣhu—in all; vedeṣhu—Vedas; brāhmaṇasya—one who realizes the Absolute Truth; vijānataḥ—who is in complete knowledge

text:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।

मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि।।2.47।।
text_kannada:
ಕರ್ಮಣ್ಯೇವಾಧಿಕಾರಸ್ತೇ ಮಾ ಫಲೇಷು ಕದಾಚನ |
ಮಾ ಕರ್ಮಫಲಹೇತೂರ್ಭೂರ್ಮಾ ತೇ ಸಂಗೋಽಸ್ತ್ವಕರ್ಮಣಿ || ೪೭ ||
text_telugu:
కర్మణ్యేవాధికారస్తే మా ఫలేషు కదాచన |
మా కర్మఫలహేతూర్భూర్మా తే సంగోఽస్త్వకర్మణి || ౪౭ ||
transliteration:
karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣhu kadāchana
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
translation_english: Your right is only to act, not to the results. Do not be the cause of the results of action. Do not have any inclination towards inaction.
translation_kannada: ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಮಾಡುವುದರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ನಿನಗೆ ಅಧಿಕಾರವಿದೆಯೇ ಹೊರತು, ಅದರ ಫಲಗಳ ಮೇಲಲ್ಲ. ಕರ್ಮದ ಫಲಕ್ಕೆ ನೀನು ಕಾರಣನಾಗಬೇಡ, ಹಾಗೆಯೇ ಕರ್ಮವನ್ನು ಮಾಡದಿರುವುದರಲ್ಲೂ ಆಸಕ್ತನಾಗಬೇಡ.
translation_telugu: నీకు కర్మ చేయుట యందు మాత్రమే అధికారము కలదు, ఆ కర్మల ఫలములపై ఎన్నడూ లేదు. కర్మఫలమునకు నీవు కారణము కాకూడదు, మరియు కర్మలు చేయకుండుట యందును నీకు ఆసక్తి కూడదు.
context_english: karmaṇi—in prescribed duties; eva—only; adhikāraḥ—right; te—your; mā—not; phaleṣhu—in the fruits; kadāchana—at any time; mā—never; karma-phala—results of the activities; hetuḥ—cause; bhūḥ—be; mā—not; te—your; saṅgaḥ—attachment; astu—must be; akarmaṇi—in inaction
context_kannada: ಇದು ಗೀತೆಯ ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ ಶ್ಲೋಕಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದಾಗಿದೆ, ಇದು ಕರ್ಮ ಯೋಗದ ಮೂಲ ತತ್ವವನ್ನು ಸ್ಥಾಪಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: ಫಲಾಪೇಕ್ಷೆಯಿಲ್ಲದ ಕ್ರಿಯೆ. ನಮ್ಮ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ನಾವು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ, ಫಲಿತಾಂಶವನ್ನಲ್ಲ.
context_telugu: ఇది గీతలోని అత్యంత ప్రసిద్ధ శ్లోకాలలో ఒకటి, ఇది కర్మ యోగం యొక్క ప్రధాన సూత్రాన్ని స్థాపిస్తుంది: ఫలాపేక్ష లేని చర్య. మన ప్రయత్నాలను మాత్రమే మనం నియంత్రిస్తాం, ఫలితాన్ని ఎప్పుడూ కాదు.

text:
योगस्थः कुरु कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा धनञ्जय।

सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योः समो भूत्वा समत्वं योग उच्यते।।2.48।।
text_kannada:
ಯೋಗಸ್ಥಃ ಕುರು ಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ಸಂಗಂ ತ್ಯಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಧನಂಜಯ |
ಸಿದ್ಧ್ಯಸಿದ್ಧ್ಯೋಃ ಸಮೋ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಸಮತ್ವಂ ಯೋಗ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ || ೪೮ ||
text_telugu:
యోగస్థః కురు కర్మాణి సంగం త్యక్త్వా ధనంజయ |
సిద్ధ్యసిద్ధ్యోః సమో భూత్వా సమత్వం యోగ ఉచ్యతే || ౪౮ ||
transliteration:
yoga-sthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṁ tyaktvā dhanañjaya
siddhy-asiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṁ yoga uchyate
translation_english: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining equanimous in success and failure. Equanimity is called Yoga.
translation_kannada: ಓ ಧನಂಜಯ, ಯೋಗದಲ್ಲಿ ನೆಲೆಸಿ, ಸಂಗವನ್ನು (ಆಸಕ್ತಿ) ಬಿಟ್ಟು, ಸಿದ್ಧಿ-ಅಸಿದ್ಧಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸಮಭಾವವುಳ್ಳವನಾಗಿ ಕರ್ಮಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡು. ಈ ಸಮತ್ವವನ್ನೇ ಯೋಗವೆಂದು ಕರೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.
translation_telugu: ఓ ధనంజయా! ఆసక్తిని విడనాడి, సిద్ధి అసిద్ధుల యందు సమత్వ బుద్ధి కలిగి యోగమునందు నిలిచి కర్మలను ఆచరింపుము. ఈ సమత్వమే యోగమనబడును.
context_english: yoga-sthaḥ—being steadfast in yog; kuru—perform; karmāṇi—duties; saṅgam—attachment; tyaktvā—having abandoned; dhanañjaya—Arjun; siddhi-asiddhyoḥ—in success and failure; samaḥ—equipoised; bhūtvā—becoming; samatvam—equanimity; yogaḥ—Yog; uchyate—is called
context_kannada: ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಕೃಷ್ಣನು ಯೋಗವನ್ನು ಭೌತಿಕ ಭಂಗಿಗಳಾಗಿ ಅಲ್ಲದೆ, ಮಾನಸಿಕ ಸಮತೋಲನದ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಎಂದು ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಯಶಸ್ಸು ಮತ್ತು ವೈಫಲ್ಯವನ್ನು ಸಮಾನವಾಗಿ ನೋಡಬೇಕು.
context_telugu: కృష్ణుడు ఇక్కడ యోగాన్ని శారీరక భంగిమలుగా కాకుండా, మానసిక సమతుల్యత స్థితిగా నిర్వచిస్తున్నాడు. విజయం మరియు వైఫల్యాన్ని సమానంగా చూడాలి.

text:
दूरेण ह्यवरं कर्म बुद्धियोगाद्धनञ्जय।

बुद्धौ शरणमन्विच्छ कृपणाः फलहेतवः।।2.49।।
text_kannada:
ದೂರೇಣ ಹ್ಯವರಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯೋಗಾದ್ಧನಂಜಯ |
ಬುದ್ಧೌ ಶರಣಮನ್ವಿಚ್ಛ ಕೃಪಣಾಃ ಫಲಹೇತವಃ || ೪೯ ||
text_telugu:
దూరేణ హ్యవరం కర్మ బుద్ధియోగాద్ధనంజయ |
బుద్ధౌ శరణమన్విచ్ఛ కృపణాః ఫలహేతవః || ౪౯ ||
transliteration:
dūreṇa hy-avaraṁ karma buddhi-yogād dhanañjaya
buddhau śharaṇam anvichchha kṛipaṇāḥ phala-hetavaḥ
translation_english: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take refuge in wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.
context_english: dūreṇa—(discrad) from far away; hi—certainly; avaram—inferior; karma—reward-seeking actions; buddhi-yogāt—with the intellect established in Divine knowledge; dhanañjaya—Arjun; buddhau—divine knowledge and insight; śharaṇam—refuge; anvichchha—seek; kṛipaṇāḥ—miserly; phala-hetavaḥ—those seeking fruits of their work

text:
बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते।

तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्।।2.50।।
text_kannada:
ಬುದ್ಧಿಯುಕ್ತೋ ಜಹಾತೀಹ ಉಭೇ ಸುಕೃತದುಷ್ಕೃತೇ |
ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯೋಗಾಯ ಯುಜ್ಯಸ್ವ ಯೋಗಃ ಕರ್ಮಸು ಕೌಶಲಮ್ || ೫೦ ||
text_telugu:
బుద్ధియుక్తో జహాతీహ ఉభే సుకృతదుష్కృతే |
తస్మాద్యోగాయ యుజ్యస్వ యోగః కర్మసు కౌశలమ్ || ౫౦ ||
transliteration:
buddhi-yukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛita-duṣhkṛite
tasmād yogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśhalam
translation_english: Possessed of wisdom, one rejects here both virtue and vice. Therefore, devote yourself to (Karma-) yoga; for yoga is skilfulness in action.
context_english: buddhi-yuktaḥ—endowed with wisdom; jahāti—get rid of; iha—in this life; ubhe—both; sukṛita-duṣhkṛite—good and bad deeds; tasmāt—therefore; yogāya—for Yog; yujyasva—strive for; yogaḥ—yog is; karmasu kauśhalam—the art of working skillfully

text:
कर्मजं बुद्धियुक्ता हि फलं त्यक्त्वा मनीषिणः।

जन्मबन्धविनिर्मुक्ताः पदं गच्छन्त्यनामयम्।।2.51।।
text_kannada:
ಕರ್ಮಜಂ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯುಕ್ತಾ ಹಿ ಫಲಂ ತ್ಯಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಮನೀಷಿಣಃ |
ಜನ್ಮಬಂಧವಿನಿರ್ಮುಕ್ತಾಃ ಪದಂ ಗಚ್ಛಂತ್ಯನಾಮಯಮ್ || ೫೧ ||
text_telugu:
కర్మజం బుద్ధియుక్తా హి ఫలం త్యక్త్వా మనీషిణః |
జన్మబంధవినిర్ముక్తాః పదం గచ్ఛంత్యనామయమ్ || ౫౧ ||
transliteration:
karma-jaṁ buddhi-yuktā hi phalaṁ tyaktvā manīṣhiṇaḥ
janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ padaṁ gachchhanty-anāmayam
translation_english: For those devoted to wisdom, they become enlightened men by giving up the fruits of their actions, and thus they reach a state beyond evil, having been freed from the bondage of birth.
context_english: karma-jam—born of fruitive actions; buddhi-yuktāḥ—endowed with equanimity of intellect; hi—as; phalam—fruits; tyaktvā—abandoning; manīṣhiṇaḥ—the wise; janma-bandha-vinirmuktāḥ—freedom from the bondage of life and death; padam—state; gachchhanti—attain; anāmayam—devoid of sufferings

text:
यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति।

तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च।।2.52।।
text_kannada:
ಯದಾ ತೇ ಮೋಹಕಲಿಲಂ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ವ್ಯತಿತರಿಷ್ಯತಿ |
ತದಾ ಗಂತಾಸಿ ನಿರ್ವೇದಂ ಶ್ರೋತವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಶ್ರುತಸ್ಯ ಚ || ೫೨ ||
text_telugu:
యదా తే మోహకలిలం బుద్ధిర్వ్యతితరిష్యతి |
తదా గంతాసి నిర్వేదం శ్రోతవ్యస్య శ్రుతస్య చ || ౫౨ ||
transliteration:
yadā te moha-kalilaṁ buddhir vyatitariṣhyati
tadā gantāsi nirvedaṁ śhrotavyasya śhrutasya cha
translation_english: When your mind goes beyond the turbidity of delusion, then you will acquire dispassion for what has to be heard and what has already been heard.
context_english: yadā—when; te—your; moha—delusion; kalilam—quagmire; buddhiḥ—intellect; vyatitariṣhyati—crosses; tadā—then; gantāsi—you shall acquire; nirvedam—indifferent; śhrotavyasya—to what is yet to be heard; śhrutasya—to what has been heard; cha—and

text:
श्रुतिविप्रतिपन्ना ते यदा स्थास्यति निश्चला।

समाधावचला बुद्धिस्तदा योगमवाप्स्यसि।।2.53।।
text_kannada:
ಶ್ರುತಿವಿಪ್ರತಿಪನ್ನಾ ತೇ ಯದಾ ಸ್ಥಾಸ್ಯತಿ ನಿಶ್ಚಲಾ |
ಸಮಾಧಾವಚಲಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿಸ್ತದಾ ಯೋಗಮವಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ || ೫೩ ||
text_telugu:
శ్రుతివిప్రతిపన్నా తే యదా స్థాస్యతి నిశ్చలా |
సమాధావచలా బుద్ధిస్తదా యోగమవాప్స్యసి || ౫౩ ||
transliteration:
śhruti-vipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niśhchalā
samādhāv-achalā buddhis tadā yogam avāpsyasi
translation_english: When your mind, which has become bewildered by hearing, becomes unshakable and steadfast in the Self, then you will attain Yoga that arises from discrimination.
context_english: śhruti-vipratipannā—not allured by the fruitive sections of the Vedas; te—your; yadā—when; sthāsyati—remains; niśhchalā—steadfast; samādhau—in divine consciousness; achalā—steadfast; buddhiḥ—intellect; tadā—at that time; yogam—Yog; avāpsyasi—you will attain

text:
अर्जुन उवाच

स्थितप्रज्ञस्य का भाषा समाधिस्थस्य केशव।

स्थितधीः किं प्रभाषेत किमासीत व्रजेत किम्।।2.54।।
text_kannada:
ಅರ್ಜುನ ಉವಾಚ |
ಸ್ಥಿತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಕಾ ಭಾಷಾ ಸಮಾಧಿಸ್ಥಸ್ಯ ಕೇಶವ |
ಸ್ಥಿತಧೀಃ ಕಿಂ ಪ್ರಭಾಷೇತ ಕಿಮಾಸೀತ ವ್ರಜೇತ ಕಿಮ್ || ೫೪ ||
text_telugu:
అర్జున ఉవాచ |
స్థితప్రజ్ఞస్య కా భాషా సమాధిస్థస్య కేశవ |
స్థితధీః కిం ప్రభాషేత కిమాసీత వ్రజేత కిమ్ || ౫౪ ||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
sthita-prajñasya kā bhāṣhā samādhi-sthasya keśhava
sthita-dhīḥ kiṁ prabhāṣheta kim āsīta vrajeta kim
translation_english: Arjuna said, "O Kesava, what is the description of a man of steady wisdom who is self-absorbed? How does he speak, sit, and move about?"
context_english: arjunaḥ uvācha—Arjun said; sthita-prajñasya—one with steady intellect; kā—what; bhāṣhā—talk; samādhi-sthasya—situated in divine consciousness; keśhava—Shree Krishna, killer of the Keshi Demon; sthita-dhīḥ—enlightened person; kim—what; prabhāṣheta—talks; kim—how; āsīta—sits; vrajeta—walks; kim—how

text:
श्री भगवानुवाच

प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्।

आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते।।2.55।।
text_kannada:
ಶ್ರೀ ಭಗವಾನುವಾಚ |
ಪ್ರಜಹಾತಿ ಯದಾ ಕಾಮಾನ್ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಮನೋಗತಾನ್ |
ಆತ್ಮನ್ಯೇವಾತ್ಮನಾ ತುಷ್ಟಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಸ್ತದೋಚ್ಯತೇ || ೫೫ ||
text_telugu:
శ్రీ భగవానువాచ |
ప్రజహాతి యదా కామాన్ సర్వాన్ పార్థ మనోగతాన్ |
ఆత్మన్యేవాత్మనా తుష్టః స్థితప్రజ్ఞస్తదోచ్యతే || ౫౫ ||
transliteration:
śhrī bhagavān uvācha
prajahāti yadā kāmān sarvān pārtha mano-gatān
ātmany-evātmanā tuṣhṭaḥ sthita-prajñas tadochyate
translation_english: The Blessed One said, "O Partha, when one fully renounces all the desires that have entered the mind and remains satisfied in the Self alone, then he is called a man of steady wisdom."
context_english: śhrī-bhagavān uvācha—The Supreme Lord said; prajahāti—discards; yadā—when; kāmān—selfish desires; sarvān—all; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; manaḥ-gatān—of the mind; ātmani—of the self; eva—only; ātmanā—by the purified mind; tuṣhṭaḥ—satisfied; sthita-prajñaḥ—one with steady intellect; tadā—at that time; uchyate—is said

text:
दुःखेष्वनुद्विग्नमनाः सुखेषु विगतस्पृहः।

वीतरागभयक्रोधः स्थितधीर्मुनिरुच्यते।।2.56।।
text_kannada:
ದುಃಖೇಷ್ವನುದ್ವಿಗ್ನಮನಾಃ ಸುಖೇಷು ವಿಗತಸ್ಪೃಹಃ |
ವೀತರಾಗಭಯಕ್ರೋಧಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಧೀರ್ಮುನಿರುಚ್ಯತೇ || ೫೬ ||
text_telugu:
దుఃఖేష్వనుద్విగ్నమనాః సుఖేషు విగతస్పృహః |
వీతరాగభయక్రోధః స్థితధీర్మునిరుచ్యతే || ౫౬ ||
transliteration:
duḥkheṣhv-anudvigna-manāḥ sukheṣhu vigata-spṛihaḥ
vīta-rāga-bhaya-krodhaḥ sthita-dhīr munir uchyate
translation_english: That monk is called a man of steady wisdom when his mind is unperturbed even in sorrow, he is free from longing for delights, and has gone beyond attachment, fear, and anger.
context_english: duḥkheṣhu—amidst miseries; anudvigna-manāḥ—one whose mind is undisturbed; sukheṣhu—in pleasure; vigata-spṛihaḥ—without craving; vīta—free from; rāga—attachment; bhaya—fear; krodhaḥ—anger; sthita-dhīḥ—enlightened person; muniḥ—a sage; uchyate—is called

text:
यः सर्वत्रानभिस्नेहस्तत्तत्प्राप्य शुभाशुभम्।

नाभिनन्दति न द्वेष्टि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.57।।
text_kannada:
ಯಃ ಸರ್ವತ್ರಾನಭಿಸ್ನೇಹಸ್ತತ್ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ಶುಭಾಶುಭಮ್ |
ನಾಭಿನಂದತಿ ನ ದ್ವೇಷ್ಟಿ ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ || ೫೭ ||
text_telugu:
యః సర్వత్రానభిస్నేహస్తత్తత్ప్రాప్య శుభాశుభమ్ |
నాభినందతి న ద్వేష్టి తస్య ప్రజ్ఞా ప్రతిష్ఠితా || ౫౭ ||
transliteration:
yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehas tat tat prāpya śhubhāśhubham
nābhinandati na dveṣhṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
translation_english: The wisdom of that person remains established who has no attachment to anything anywhere, who neither welcomes nor rejects anything, whatever good or bad, when they come across it.
context_english: yaḥ—who; sarvatra—in all conditions; anabhisnehaḥ—unattached; tat—that; tat—that; prāpya—attaining; śhubha—good; aśhubham—evil; na—neither; abhinandati—delight in; na—nor; dveṣhṭi—dejected by; tasya—his; prajñā—knowledge; pratiṣhṭhitā—is fixed

text:
यदा संहरते चायं कूर्मोऽङ्गानीव सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.58।।
text_kannada:
ಯದಾ ಸಂಹರತೇ ಚಾಯಂ ಕೂರ್ಮೋಽಂಗಾನೀವ ಸರ್ವಶಃ |
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣೀಂದ್ರಿಯಾರ್ಥೇಭ್ಯಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ || ೫೮ ||
text_telugu:
యదా సంహరతే చాయం కూర్మోఽంగానీవ సర్వశః |
ఇంద్రియాణీంద్రియార్థేభ్యస్తస్య ప్రజ్ఞా ప్రతిష్ఠితా || ౫౮ ||
transliteration:
yadā sanharate chāyaṁ kūrmo ’ṅgānīva sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
translation_english: And when one fully withdraws their senses from the objects of the senses, just as a tortoise withdraws its limbs, then their wisdom remains established.
context_english: yadā—when; sanharate—withdraw; cha—and; ayam—this; kūrmaḥ—tortoise; aṅgāni—limbs; iva—as; sarvaśhaḥ—fully; indriyāṇi—senses; indriya-arthebhyaḥ—from the sense objects; tasya—his; prajñā—divine wisdom; pratiṣhṭhitā—fixed in

text:
विषया विनिवर्तन्ते निराहारस्य देहिनः।

रसवर्जं रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते।।2.59।।
text_kannada:
ವಿಷಯಾ ವಿನಿವರ್ತಂತೇ ನಿರಾಹಾರಸ್ಯ ದೇಹಿನಃ |
ರಸವರ್ಜಂ ರಸೋಽಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಪರಂ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ನಿವರ್ತತೇ || ೫೯ ||
text_telugu:
విషయా వినివర్తంతే నిరాహారస్య దేహినః |
రసవర్జం రసోఽప్యస్య పరం దృష్ట్వా నివర్తతే || ౫౯ ||
transliteration:
viṣhayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ
rasa-varjaṁ raso ’pyasya paraṁ dṛiṣhṭvā nivartate
translation_english: The objects recede from an abstinent person, except for the taste for them. Even this taste falls away after realization of the Absolute.
context_english: viṣhayāḥ—objects for senses; vinivartante—restrain; nirāhārasya—practicing self restraint; dehinaḥ—for the embodied; rasa-varjam—cessation of taste; rasaḥ—taste; api—however; asya—person’s; param—the Supreme; dṛiṣhṭvā—on realization; nivartate—ceases to be

text:
यततो ह्यपि कौन्तेय पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः।

इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि हरन्ति प्रसभं मनः।।2.60।।
text_kannada:
ಯತತೋ ಹ್ಯಪಿ ಕೌಂತೇಯ ಪುರುಷಸ್ಯ ವಿಪಶ್ಚಿತಃ |
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಥೀನಿ ಹರಂತಿ ಪ್ರಸಭಂ ಮನಃ || ೬೦ ||
text_telugu:
యతతో హ్యపి కౌంతేయ పురుషస్య విపశ్చితః |
ఇంద్రియాణి ప్రమాథీని హరంతి ప్రసభం మనః || ౬౦ ||
transliteration:
yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣhasya vipaśhchitaḥ
indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṁ manaḥ
translation_english: For, O son of Kunti, the turbulent senses can violently snatch away the mind of an intelligent person, even while they are striving diligently.
context_english: yatataḥ—while practicing self-control; hi—for; api—even; kaunteya—Arjun, the son of Kunti; puruṣhasya—of a person; vipaśhchitaḥ—one endowed with discrimination; indriyāṇi—the senses; pramāthīni—turbulent; haranti—carry away; prasabham—forcibly; manaḥ—the mind

text:
तानि सर्वाणि संयम्य युक्त आसीत मत्परः।

वशे हि यस्येन्द्रियाणि तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.61।।
text_kannada:
ತಾನಿ ಸರ್ವಾಣಿ ಸಂಯಮ್ಯ ಯುಕ್ತ ಆಸೀತ ಮತ್ಪರಃ |
ವಶೇ ಹಿ ಯಸ್ಯೇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ || ೬೧ ||
text_telugu:
తాని సర్వాణి సంయమ్య యుక్త ఆసీత మత్పరః |
వశే హి యస్యేంద్రియాణి తస్య ప్రజ్ఞా ప్రతిష్ఠితా || ౬౧ ||
transliteration:
tāni sarvāṇi sanyamya yukta āsīta mat-paraḥ
vaśhe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
translation_english: Controlling all of them, one should remain focused on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose senses are under control becomes steadfast.
context_english: tāni—them; sarvāṇi—all; sanyamya—subduing; yuktaḥ—united; āsīta—seated; mat-paraḥ—toward me (Shree Krishna); vaśhe—control; hi—certainly; yasya—whose; indriyāṇi—senses; tasya—their; prajñā—perfect knowledge pratiṣhṭhitā

text:
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।

सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते।।2.62।।
text_kannada:
ಧ್ಯಾಯತೋ ವಿಷಯಾನ್ಪುಂಸಃ ಸಂಗಸ್ತೇಷೂಪಜಾಯತೇ |
ಸಂಗಾತ್ ಸಂಜಾಯತೇ ಕಾಮಃ ಕಾಮಾತ್ಕ್ರೋಧೋಽಭಿಜಾಯತೇ || ೬೨ ||
text_telugu:
ధ్యాయతో విషయాన్పుంసః సంగస్తేషూపజాయతే |
సంగాత్ సంజాయతే కామః కామాత్క్రోధోఽభిజాయతే || ౬౨ ||
transliteration:
dhyāyato viṣhayān puṁsaḥ saṅgas teṣhūpajāyate
saṅgāt sañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmāt krodho ’bhijāyate
translation_english: - In the case of a person who dwells on objects, there arises attachment to them. From attachment grows hankering, and from hankering springs anger.
context_english: dhyāyataḥ—contemplating; viṣhayān—sense objects; puṁsaḥ—of a person; saṅgaḥ—attachment; teṣhu—to them (sense objects); upajāyate—arises; saṅgāt—from attachment; sañjāyate—develops; kāmaḥ—desire; kāmāt—from desire; krodhaḥ—anger; abhijāyate—arises

text:
क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।

स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति।।2.63।।
text_kannada:
ಕ್ರೋಧಾದ್ಭವತಿ ಸಂಮೋಹಃ ಸಂಮೋಹಾತ್ಸ್ಮೃತಿವಿಭ್ರಮಃ |
ಸ್ಮೃತಿಭ್ರಂಶಾದ್ ಬುದ್ಧಿನಾಶೋ ಬುದ್ಧಿನಾಶಾತ್ಪ್ರಣಶ್ಯತಿ || ೬೩ ||
text_telugu:
క్రోధాద్భవతి సంమోహః సంమోహాత్స్మృతివిభ్రమః |
స్మృతిభ్రంశాద్ బుద్ధినాశో బుద్ధినాశాత్ప్రణశ్యతి || ౬౩ ||
transliteration:
krodhād bhavati sammohaḥ sammohāt smṛiti-vibhramaḥ
smṛiti-bhranśhād buddhi-nāśho buddhi-nāśhāt praṇaśhyati
translation_english: From anger follows delusion; from delusion, a failure of memory; from the failure of memory, the loss of understanding; and from the loss of understanding, one perishes.
context_english: krodhāt—from anger; bhavati—comes; sammohaḥ—clouding of judgement; sammohāt—from clouding of judgement; smṛiti—memory; vibhramaḥ—bewilderment; smṛiti-bhranśhāt—from bewilderment of memory; buddhi-nāśhaḥ—destruction of intellect; buddhi-nāśhāt—from destruction of intellect; praṇaśhyati—one is ruined

text:
रागद्वेषवियुक्तैस्तु विषयानिन्द्रियैश्चरन्।

आत्मवश्यैर्विधेयात्मा प्रसादमधिगच्छति।।2.64।।
text_kannada:
ರಾಗದ್ವೇಷವಿಯುಕ್ತೈಸ್ತು ವಿಷಯಾನಿಂದ್ರಿಯೈಶ್ಚರನ್ |
ಆತ್ಮವಶ್ಯೈರ್ವಿಧೇಯಾತ್ಮಾ ಪ್ರಸಾದಮಧಿಗಚ್ಛತಿ || ೬೪ ||
text_telugu:
రాగద్వేషవియుక్తైస్తు విషయానింద్రియైశ్చరన్ |
ఆత్మవశ్యైర్విధేయాత్మా ప్రసాదమధిగచ్ఛతి || ౬౪ ||
transliteration:
rāga-dveṣha-viyuktais tu viṣhayān indriyaiśh charan
ātma-vaśhyair-vidheyātmā prasādam adhigachchhati
translation_english: But by perceiving objects with the organs that are free from attraction and repulsion, and are under his own control, the self-controlled person attains serenity.
context_english: rāga—attachment; dveṣha—aversion; viyuktaiḥ—free; tu—but; viṣhayān—objects of the senses; indriyaiḥ—by the senses; charan—while using; ātma-vaśhyaiḥ—controlling one’s mind; vidheya-ātmā—one who controls the mind; prasādam—the Grace of God; adhigachchhati—attains

text:
प्रसादे सर्वदुःखानां हानिरस्योपजायते।

प्रसन्नचेतसो ह्याशु बुद्धिः पर्यवतिष्ठते।।2.65।।
text_kannada:
ಪ್ರಸಾದೇ ಸರ್ವದುಃಖಾನಾಂ ಹಾನಿರಸ್ಯೋಪಜಾಯತೇ |
ಪ್ರಸನ್ನಚೇತಸೋ ಹ್ಯಾಶು ಬುದ್ಧಿಃ ಪರ್ಯವತಿಷ್ಠತೇ || ೬೫ ||
text_telugu:
ప్రసాదే సర్వదుఃఖానాం హానిరస్యోపజాయతే |
ప్రసన్నచేతసో హ్యాశు బుద్ధిః పర్యవతిష్ఠతే || ౬౫ ||
transliteration:
prasāde sarva-duḥkhānāṁ hānir asyopajāyate
prasanna-chetaso hyāśhu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣhṭhate
translation_english: When there is serenity, all his sorrows are eradicated, for the wisdom of one with a serene mind soon becomes firmly established.
context_english: prasāde—by divine grace; sarva—all; duḥkhānām—of sorrows; hāniḥ—destruction; asya—his; upajāyate—comes; prasanna-chetasaḥ—with a tranquil mind; hi—indeed; āśhu—soon; buddhiḥ—intellect; paryavatiṣhṭhate—becomes firmly established

text:
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना।

न चाभावयतः शान्तिरशान्तस्य कुतः सुखम्।।2.66।।
text_kannada:
ನಾಸ್ತಿ ಬುದ್ಧಿರಯುಕ್ತಸ್ಯ ನ ಚಾಯುಕ್ತಸ್ಯ ಭಾವನಾ |
ನ ಚಾಭಾವಯತಃ ಶಾಂತಿರಶಾಂತಸ್ಯ ಕುತಃ ಸುಖಮ್ || ೬೬ ||
text_telugu:
నాస్తి బుద్ధిరయుక్తస్య న చాయుక్తస్య భావనా |
న చాభావయతః శాంతిరశాంతస్య కుతః సుఖమ్ || ౬౬ ||
transliteration:
nāsti buddhir-ayuktasya na chāyuktasya bhāvanā
na chābhāvayataḥ śhāntir aśhāntasya kutaḥ sukham
translation_english: For the unsteady there is no wisdom, and there is no meditation for the unsteady person. And for an unmeditative person there is no peace. How can there be happiness for one without peace?
context_english: na—not; asti—is; buddhiḥ—intellect; ayuktasya—not united; na—not; cha—and; ayuktasya—not united; bhāvanā—contemplation; na—nor; cha—and; abhāvayataḥ—for those not united; śhāntiḥ—peace; aśhāntasya—of the unpeaceful; kutaḥ—where; sukham—happiness

text:
इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते।

तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि।।2.67।।
text_kannada:
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣಾಂ ಹಿ ಚರತಾಂ ಯನ್ಮನೋಽನುವಿಧೀಯತೇ |
ತದಸ್ಯ ಹರತಿ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾಂ ವಾಯುರ್ನಾವಮಿವಾಂಭಸಿ || ೬೭ ||
text_telugu:
ఇంద్రియాణాం హి చరతాం యన్మనోఽనువిధీయతే |
తదస్య హరతి ప్రజ్ఞాం వాయుర్నావమివాంభసి || ౬౭ ||
transliteration:
indriyāṇāṁ hi charatāṁ yan mano ’nuvidhīyate
tadasya harati prajñāṁ vāyur nāvam ivāmbhasi
translation_english: For, the mind which follows in the wake of the wandering senses carries away his wisdom like a boat on the waters.
context_english: indriyāṇām—of the senses; hi—indeed; charatām—roaming; yat—which; manaḥ—the mind; anuvidhīyate—becomes constantly engaged; tat—that; asya—of that; harati—carries away; prajñām—intellect; vāyuḥ—wind; nāvam—boat; iva—as; ambhasi—on the water

text:
तस्माद्यस्य महाबाहो निगृहीतानि सर्वशः।

इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थेभ्यस्तस्य प्रज्ञा प्रतिष्ठिता।।2.68।।
text_kannada:
ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಮಹಾಬಾಹೋ ನಿಗೃಹೀತಾನಿ ಸರ್ವಶಃ |
ಇಂದ್ರಿಯಾಣೀಂದ್ರಿಯಾರ್ಥೇಭ್ಯಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ || ೬೮ ||
text_telugu:
తస్మాద్యస్య మహాబాహో నిగృహీతాని సర్వశః |
ఇంద్రియాణీంద్రియార్థేభ్యస్తస్య ప్రజ్ఞా ప్రతిష్ఠితా || ౬౮ ||
transliteration:
tasmād yasya mahā-bāho nigṛihītāni sarvaśhaḥ
indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyas tasya prajñā pratiṣhṭhitā
translation_english: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, this wisdom becomes established when all its senses are withdrawn from their objects.
context_english: tasmāt—therefore; yasya—whose; mahā-bāho—mighty-armed one; nigṛihītāni—restrained; sarvaśhaḥ—completely; indriyāṇi—senses; indriya-arthebhyaḥ—from sense objects; tasya—of that person; prajñā—transcendental knowledge; pratiṣhṭhitā—remains fixed

text:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी।

यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः।।2.69।।
text_kannada:
ಯಾ ನಿಶಾ ಸರ್ವಭೂತಾನಾಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಂ ಜಾಗರ್ತಿ ಸಂಯಮೀ |
ಯಸ್ಯಾಂ ಜಾಗ್ರತಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ಸಾ ನಿಶಾ ಪಶ್ಯತೋ ಮುನೇಃ || ೬೯ ||
text_telugu:
యా నిశా సర్వభూతానాం తస్యాం జాగర్తి సంయమీ |
యస్యాం జాగ్రతి భూతాని సా నిశా పశ్యతో మునేః || ౬౯ ||
transliteration:
yā niśhā sarva-bhūtānāṁ tasyāṁ jāgarti sanyamī
yasyāṁ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśhā paśhyato muneḥ
translation_english: The self-restrained man stays awake during what is night for all creatures. That which creatures stay awake for, it is night to the discerning sage.
context_english: yā—which; niśhā—night; sarva-bhūtānām—of all living beings; tasyām—in that; jāgarti—is awake; sanyamī—self-controlled; yasyām—in which; jāgrati—are awake; bhūtāni—creatures; sā—that; niśhā—night; paśhyataḥ—see; muneḥ—sage

text:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं

समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत्।

तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे

स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी।।2.70।।
text_kannada:
ಆಪೂರ್ಯಮಾಣಮಚಲಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಂ |
ಸಮುದ್ರಮಾಪಃ ಪ್ರವಿಶಂತಿ ಯದ್ವತ್ |
ತದ್ವತ್ಕಾಮಾ ಯಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶಂತಿ ಸರ್ವೇ |
ಸ ಶಾಂತಿಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ನ ಕಾಮಕಾಮೀ || ೭೦ ||
text_telugu:
ఆపూర్యమాణమచలప్రతిష్ఠం |
సముద్రమాపః ప్రవిశంతి యద్వత్ |
తద్వత్కామా యం ప్రవిశంతి సర్వే |
స శాంతిమాప్నోతి న కామకామీ || ౭౦ ||
transliteration:
āpūryamāṇam achala-pratiṣhṭhaṁ
samudram āpaḥ praviśhanti yadvat
tadvat kāmā yaṁ praviśhanti sarve
sa śhāntim āpnoti na kāma-kāmī
translation_english: That man attains peace into whom all desires enter, just as waters flow into the sea that remains unchanged even when filled from all sides. Not so one who is desirous of objects.
context_english: āpūryamāṇam—filled from all sides; achala-pratiṣhṭham—undisturbed; samudram—ocean; āpaḥ—waters; praviśhanti—enter; yadvat—as; tadvat—likewise; kāmāḥ—desires; yam—whom; praviśhanti—enter; sarve—all; saḥ—that person; śhāntim—peace; āpnoti—attains; na—not; kāma-kāmī—one who strives to satisfy desires

text:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमांश्चरति निःस्पृहः।

निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शांतिमधिगच्छति।।2.71।।
text_kannada:
ವಿಹಾಯ ಕಾಮಾನ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪುಮಾಂಶ್ಚರತಿ ನಿಃಸ್ಪೃಹಃ |
ನಿರ್ಮಮೋ ನಿರಹಂಕಾರಃ ಸ ಶಾಂತಿಮಧಿಗಚ್ಛತಿ || ೭೧ ||
text_telugu:
విహాయ కామాన్యః సర్వాన్పుమాంశ్చరతి నిఃస్పృహః |
నిర్మమో నిరహంకారః స శాంతిమధిగచ్ఛతి || ౭౧ ||
transliteration:
vihāya kāmān yaḥ sarvān pumānśh charati niḥspṛihaḥ
nirmamo nirahankāraḥ sa śhāntim adhigachchhati
translation_english: That man attains peace who, after rejecting all desires, moves about free from hankering, without the idea of 'me' and 'mine', and devoid of pride.
context_english: vihāya—giving up; kāmān—material desires; yaḥ—who; sarvān—all; pumān—a person; charati—lives; niḥspṛihaḥ—free from hankering; nirmamaḥ—without a sense of proprietorship; nirahankāraḥ—without egoism; saḥ—that person; śhāntim—perfect peace; adhigachchhati—attains

text:
एषा ब्राह्मी स्थितिः पार्थ नैनां प्राप्य विमुह्यति।

स्थित्वाऽस्यामन्तकालेऽपि ब्रह्मनिर्वाणमृच्छति।।2.72।।
text_kannada:
ಏಷಾ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮೀ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ನೈನಾಂ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ವಿಮುಹ್ಯತಿ |
ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾಽಸ್ಯಾಮಂತಕಾಲೇಽಪಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿರ್ವಾಣಮೃಚ್ಛತಿ || ೭೨ ||
text_telugu:
ఏషా బ్రాహ్మీ స్థితిః పార్థ నైనాం ప్రాప్య విముహ్యతి |
స్థిత్వాఽస్యామంతకాలేఽపి బ్రహ్మనిర్వాణమృచ్ఛతి || ౭౨ ||
transliteration:
eṣhā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṁ prāpya vimuhyati
sthitvāsyām anta-kāle ’pi brahma-nirvāṇam ṛichchhati
translation_english: O Partha, this is the state of being established in Brahman. One does not become deluded after attaining this; one attains identification with Brahman by being established in this state even in the closing years of one's life.
context_english: eṣhā—such; brāhmī sthitiḥ—state of God-realization; pārtha—Arjun, the son of Pritha; na—never; enām—this; prāpya—having attained; vimuhyati—is deluded; sthitvā—being established; asyām—in this; anta-kāle—at the hour of death; api—even; brahma-nirvāṇam—liberation from Maya; ṛichchhati—attains

text:
अर्जुन उवाच

ज्यायसी चेत्कर्मणस्ते मता बुद्धिर्जनार्दन।

तत्किं कर्मणि घोरे मां नियोजयसि केशव।।3.1।।
text_kannada:
ಅರ್ಜುನ ಉವಾಚ |
ಜ್ಯಾಯಸೀ ಚೇತ್ಕರ್ಮಣಸ್ತೇ ಮತಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ಜನಾರ್ದನ |
ತತ್ಕಿಂ ಕರ್ಮಣಿ ಘೋರೇ ಮಾಂ ನಿಯೋಜಯಸಿ ಕೇಶವ || ೧ ||
text_telugu:
అర్జున ఉవాచ |
జ్యాయసీ చేత్కర్మణస్తే మతా బుద్ధిర్జనార్దన |
తత్కిం కర్మణి ఘోరే మాం నియోజయసి కేశవ || ౧ ||
transliteration:
arjuna uvācha
jyāyasī chet karmaṇas te matā buddhir janārdana
tat kiṁ karmaṇi ghore māṁ niyojayasi keśhava
translation_english: Arjuna said, "O Janardana (Krishna), if it is Your opinion that wisdom is superior to action, why do You urge me to take such horrible action, O Kesava?"
